description: The judgement of the example audit: every difference with its severity and status, the lint triage, and what was not checked. Written by make-decisions.py; read by tools/build-example-audit.mjs.

label-colon-missing.note: A Windows 95 label for a field ends with a colon. Left for the owner: wording.

button-title-caps.note: Windows 95 capitalises each word of a button label. Left for the owner: wording.

menu-title-caps.note: Windows 95 capitalises each word of a menu command. Left for the owner: wording.

dialog-title-caps.note: Windows 95 capitalises each word of a title. Left for the owner: wording.

ellipsis-character.note: Windows 95 wrote three full stops; the single ellipsis character is later. Left for the owner: wording, and the example checks match on the text.

period-vocabulary.note: The finding is the page's own heading, written for today's reader, not interface text of the sample.

window-too-large.note: The example dialogs are 460 px wide, set by the page layer; 263 dialog units is the guideline's limit for a 640 by 480 screen.

no-default-button.note: The question has no default button; Keep editing has the initial focus instead.

button-width-mismatch.note: Two buttons in a row sized by their labels; Windows 95 gives a row one width.

buttons.counterpart: OK, Cancel and Apply in a real dialog and property sheet (user32)

differences.exampleDoes: Create keeps the default look while Reset has the focus.
differences.note: The kit now does this inside a dialog (fixed in the modal example). This page is a form on a page, not a dialog, and Windows only does it in dialogs.

differences.summary: Buttons are 8 px apart and as wide as their labels.
differences.real: Buttons in a row 4 dialog units (6 px) apart, each 50 units (75 px) wide.
differences.exampleDoes: 8 px apart; width from the label.
